ornament.hint: Decorative borders, with the same text size and spacing. Corner flourishes appear where there is room.
ornament.frameHint: An interwoven elven frame reserves space around the text. Fitting and page count may change.
ornament.lowInk: Low ink uses the classic rules. Your style returns in colour or monochrome.
_note: Source of truth for every UI string. Other catalogues in this directory are partial overlays; a key they omit falls back to the English here. Keys are namespaced by where the string appears. {name} is a placeholder filled at runtime.
cut.hint.cut: Cut each sheet down the middle: four double-sided cards from every four faces.
cut.hint.fold: Fold each sheet down the middle: every four faces make one four-panel card. The panels print out of order so they read 1-2-3-4 once folded; a tick at each edge marks the crease.
cut.hint.longEdge: Your printer turns the sheet top over bottom, so each back is pre-rotated.
cut.hint.shortEdge: Your printer turns the sheet like a book page, so the back comes out upright.
cut.hint.whole: Print double-sided. Each sheet is one face on the front, one on the back.

format.backgroundTitle.sections: Each section's own colour, under the rows it belongs to

format.entryLayoutLong: How each entry is laid out
format.fitTitle: Fit the type to the faces you asked for
format.head: Header / footer
format.headFillTitle.none: No tab. The band is type on the paper.
format.headFillTitle.one: The same colour on every face, whichever sections land on it.
format.headReachTitle.band: The band’s own strip, projecting in from the side, with paper still above it.
format.headReachTitle.corner: Run on to the top or bottom edge of the face, so the colour fills the corner.
format.headReachTitle.edge: The corner, plus a rail of the same colour down the outside of the column for the whole height of the face, so a fanned stack can be read from the side. It runs in the margin, so the column’s own words stay on white. A middle tab has no outer edge to run down and gets the corner alone.
format.headSpanTitle.center: Everything gathered into the middle instead of spread across the face.
format.headSpanTitle.full: The three positions spread across the width, as a running head normally is.
format.headSpanTitle.left: Everything gathered into the left corner instead of spread across the face.
format.headSpanTitle.right: Everything gathered into the right corner instead of spread across the face.
format.phoneLong: Which phone the wallpaper is for
format.reserveBottom: Clear at the bottom, in percent
format.reserveHint: A lock screen draws the clock and date across the top and its buttons across the bottom. These bands leave that space empty, so no word on the card ends up under them.
format.reserveTitle: {top}% clear at the top, {bottom}% at the bottom
format.reserveTop: Clear at the top, in percent
format.splitLong: Where the divider between an entry’s two halves sits
format.splitTitle.adaptive: Each row sets its own — fits more words, worth 5–23% larger type, and moves the divider from row to row
format.splitTitle.consistent: One divider for a whole section, so its rows line up

warn.break-failed: At {scale}x the content does not fit, across {columns} columns in total.
warn.card-too-small: Even {faces} faces of this card leave the type near its smallest readable size. A larger card, or fewer sections, would read better.
warn.emergency-unreviewed: The emergency numbers on file for {region} have not been checked by a fluent speaker, so they are left off the sheet. Verify them and raise their confidence, or add your own with the CSV import.
warn.empty-column: The {field} column is switched on, but nothing on this sheet has one, so it prints nothing. Fill it in with the CSV import, or switch the column off.
warn.hairline-too-thin: The thinnest rule is {thinnest}pt, below the {minimum}pt this paper can hold. It may print as nothing. Try photo stock, or a theme with heavier rules.
warn.ink-mode.lowInk: Low ink drops the row shading, which makes long tables harder to follow across the section coding.
warn.ink-mode.mono: Mono drops both colour and shading, so sections are told apart by their icons and titles alone.
warn.loose-columns: Some columns could not be filled evenly ({count}). Try “Balance columns” to propose items that would take up the space.
warn.margin-below-safe-area: Margins were widened to {inset}pt to stay inside the {preset} printable area.
warn.no-dictionary-breaking: {script} needs dictionary line breaking, which is not implemented yet; lines may break mid-word.
warn.no-emergency-numbers: No emergency numbers on file for {region}. Look them up before you travel and add them with the CSV import.
warn.no-fit.auto: Even {faces} faces will not hold this at a legible size, at {columns} columns per face.
warn.no-fit.pinned: The content will not fit {faces} faces at {columns} columns per face without going below a legible size.
warn.nothing-selected: Nothing is selected, so the sheet is blank. Switch a section back on in the content panel.
warn.paper-too-coarse: This paper needs {script} text at {floor}pt, but the theme sets its {field} column at {size}pt. That column is enlarged to stay readable, which costs room elsewhere. Photo stock holds finer type.

speaker.title: How you speak
speaker.lede: Some languages change a sentence depending on who is saying it. Answer once here and every phrase will be in your own voice — on the board, on the cheat sheet and in the practice drills. Nothing is guessed, and nothing leaves this device.
speaker.unspecified: Rather not say — use the standard wording
speaker.nothingToAsk: Neither of these languages changes a phrase according to who is speaking, so there is nothing to set.
speaker.unset: {axes}: not set, so these phrases use the standard wording.
speaker.speaker_gender.why: In these languages a verb or an adjective about yourself changes form. “I am lost” and “thank you” are different sentences depending on the answer.
speech.no-voice: This device has no voice for that language.
speech.remote-only: The only voice for that language needs a connection.
speech.loading: Voices are still loading — try again in a moment.
speech.unsupported: This browser cannot read text aloud.
speech.unmapped: There is no voice for that language anywhere.
speech.synthesis-failed: The voice stopped. Try again, or show the text.

signal.heading: Signal in Morse
signal.lede: Type what you need to say. The phone flashes it — the screen, and the lamp where the phone will lend it — in Morse, at a speed a person can read. SOS is one tap.
